Type foundry arm of Our Polite Society, a design practice formed 2008 by Jens Schildt and Matthias Kreutzer; members across Stockholm, Hamburg and Montreal (previously Amsterdam). Retail and custom typefaces: Favorite, Placard, Cubic, Facitype (the FACIT Model project draws on Swedish office-machine ephemera), plus Grotesko, Past Perfect, Capitalis Brutalis, Noise Abroad, And Ever, And Ever Ultra, Used Future, Kappla, Restructional Text. 13 typefaces in the catalog as of 2025. Foundry (type house) for this entry; the parent OPS is a broader graphic/identity studio. Small distributed team (Size 2-10). Reviewed on Typographica and Fonts in Use; the Facitype FACIT project was covered by Creative Boom. Website updated to ops-type.com (the live canonical URL; ourpolitesocietytype.net permanently redirects there). Email info@ops-type.com confirmed on the ops-type.com About page. LinkedIn: company page found at linkedin.com/company/our-polite-society; no personal LinkedIn profiles for either founder confirmed at >=0.8. Work captured as screenshots of the foundry live interactive specimen viewer (no static raster images on the site; each typeface is rendered in the browser as a live type tester) plus archival project images from the Creative Boom Facit Model article. text.content: Should we work with them? Yes. Seems very capable. A bit restrained but makes up for it in his professionalism in spades. Comes from a design background (15 years), saw the need to learn more about development; finding it easier to find work as a developer. Very focused on interactive and creative 'memorable' user experience: 'provide a better experience for the user' (love that he says that). Shopify and ecommerce especially. Really focused on website performance. Considers himself a 'Creative' developer. Talks about opportunities to give things life. 'I don't want my clients to spend extra money if not needed.' 'If we need to change things, that's fine, it's part of the job.' Likes to bring everyone together to brainstorm and prep. Stack: Prismic, Vue.js, Nuxt.js (main); Prismic/WP/Magento/Contentful; Vue/Nuxt/React; Node.js/Express; Shopify; Pixi.js, GreenSock, Three.js, WebGL. Freelance full-time, Toronto. Hourly 75USD/hr, day rate 600USD/d. Process: 1) basic HTML/CSS, finish the design; 2) animations, interaction; 3) cross-browser. Example proposal: proposal.by-victorwork.com/sleau.

Mária Švarbová (b. 1988, Zlaté Moravce, Slovakia) is a fine-art photographer and art director based in Bratislava, Slovakia. She is known for her symmetrical, pastel-toned conceptual series set in socialist-era architecture (most famously her Swimming Pool series, 2014 onward), which won the 2018 Hasselblad Masters Award in the Fine Art category. Her work has appeared in Vogue, Forbes, CNN and The Guardian, and she has shot advertising campaigns for Apple, Murata and Museum of Ice Cream; she was listed in Forbes Slovakia 30 Under 30 in 2017. She works independently as a self-employed photographer/art director, commissioning her own fine-art series and taking on commercial projects on a per-project basis (no evidence of employment). Gallery representation includes Contessa Gallery and Gilman Contemporary; prints available via Artsy. Seniority: established mid-career independent, roughly 15 years of active practice with significant international gallery presence and commercial credits. Autonomy 4: highly self-directed creative vision, owns all creative decisions; occasionally directs commercial work for large clients, but works alone rather than leading a permanent team. Dunne and Raby (Anthony Dunne + Fiona Raby) is a two-person speculative and critical design practice founded in 1994, widely regarded as the originators of Critical Design and Speculative Design as fields. Practice based in UK (London) with extended US presence; 2016-2025 they were University Professors of Design and Social Inquiry at Parsons / The New School in New York, co-directing the Designed Realities Studio. As of 2025, Distinguished Visiting Professors at the China Academy of Art. Historically at the RCA: Anthony as Professor and Head of Design Interactions (2005-2015), Fiona as Reader in Design Interactions. Very senior, field-defining level: ~32 years of practice, four books (Hertzian Tales 1999, Design Noir 2001, Speculative Everything 2013, Not Here, Not Now 2025), work in MoMA and V and A permanent collections. MIT Media Lab Award 2015 inaugural recipients, Royal Designers for Industry 2021. Autonomy: 5 (fully autonomous; run their own studio and set their own agenda; academic chairs). Work Status=Studio confirmed: dunneandraby.co.uk is their active studio site. No Instagram context shot: no confirmed studio handle exists; two personal handles (@anthony__dunne, @ny__f) surfaced in search results but not verified against bios and left as an Open Question.

Typefaces are drawn from the history of social and civil-rights movements (Civil Rights Movement, women's suffrage, Stonewall, the Chicano Moratorium), explicitly positioned around diversity in type and giving underrepresented creatives a voice in the industry. UNKNOWN (unknown-type.com) is a free contemporary display typeface, and the small foundry/microsite behind it, released March 2020 by Austrian graphic designers Lukas Haider (Graz, based Vienna, ex-Studio Great, now runs his own studio) and Alexander Raffl (Vienna, works at HammerAlbrecht). The typeface ships in three styles (RND, PX, MX) with about 1,125 glyphs and stylistic alternates; used in Broad Leaf Spirits packaging, Madame magazine and other projects per Fonts In Use. Reads as a two-person passion project rather than an ongoing studio: unknown-type.com is currently dead (parked "coming soon" page), no dedicated foundry Instagram or LinkedIn found after a few searches, only the designers' personal Behance/IG (Lukas Haider: @lkshdr).

Work capture: site was dead so images were pulled from the designers' own Behance project page (specimens, full res) and Fonts In Use (real in-use applications: Broad Leaf Spirits vodka packaging, Madame magazine cover, TAU 365 merch), each eyeballed to confirm the UNKNOWN typeface. Context anchor is a screenshot of the Fonts In Use foundry page, not the dead site or Behance: unknown-type.com renders blank/"OK" in a headless browser despite curl showing the real parked page (parking-service bot handling quirk), and the Behance project page hit an Adobe rate limit ("maximum number of requests exceeded") on two tries. No Instagram attached per the open question (none dedicated to the foundry; only the designers' personal accounts).

Historically family owned and North America's largest privately held fine paper maker, acquired by Fedrigoni in Feb 2024. Known for Mohawk Superfine and Strathmore paper lines, sold to designers, brands and printers rather than doing creative work itself; likely 1000+ staff (some sources put mill + corporate near 700-1100), set Size to 100+ as a hedge.

Tried twice per the time-box, confirmed the block is site-wide, not a single blocked path. Fix for a future pass: a human-driven browser session (Jonathan's own Chrome) could clear the challenge once and let a saved cookie through, or ask Mohawk for a press/media kit. Captured the on-capability "Paper & materials" work instead from their Instagram (@mohawkpaper, active brand account, 27.3K followers): 10 images spanning three ranges, Mohawk Mosaic (swatches, texture/foil detail, swatchbook cover, a die-cut hotel-tag promo piece), Mohawk Digital (paper stock spec close-up, gradient print poster with paper specs, a promo card, swatchbooks), plus a general Fedrigoni x Mohawk paper-stack brand shot and a shelf of product swatchbooks. Rejected a composite grid image (redundant with the individually captured Digital pieces) and an off-capability event/people photo (Mohawk Converge Summit). Logged-out capture only got ~640px images; queued to state/ig-queue.json for a future logged-in ig.py pass to pull true full-res.
